evidence.title: Scioto Hopewell Mound Group (Ohio): 2,500-km Rocky Mountain Obsidian to Gulf Whelk Hub
evidence.dateBasis: XRF Yellowstone obsidian, Lake Superior copper, Ontario silver & Blue Ridge mica
evidence.summary: Scioto Valley earthworks assembled raw volcanic glass from Yellowstone and Bear Gulch, Michigan copper, Ontario native silver, Appalachian mica, and Florida Gulf shells into monumental ritual craft.
evidence.limits: Sourced raw materials document directional supply spheres rather than single-caravan schedules.

evidence.title: Poverty Point Earthworks (Louisiana): Late Archaic Forager Continental Stone & Metal Web
evidence.dateBasis: Ouachita quartz, Missouri galena/chert, Appalachian soapstone & eastern copper
evidence.summary: Mobile fisher-hunter-gatherers at Poverty Point imported metric tons of non-local stone, copper beads, and marine shells across 1,000+ km river basins well before farming villages.
evidence.limits: Absence of centralized hierarchy underscores episodic ceremonial gathering exchange.

evidence.title: San Lorenzo & La Venta (Olmec Gulf Coast): Motagua Jadeite, Oaxaca Mirrors & Ilmenite
evidence.dateBasis: PIXE Guatemalan Motagua jadeite, Oaxaca magnetite & Chiapas ilmenite caches
evidence.summary: Gulf Coast Olmec workshops imported Guatemalan jadeite celts, Highland Oaxaca optical iron-ore mirrors, and tons of Isthmian ilmenite cubes alongside El Chayal and Hidalgo obsidian.
evidence.limits: Alluvial sources in secondary Motagua tributaries remain under survey.

evidence.title: Chavín de Huántar & Caral-Supe (Peru): Ecuadorian Spondylus, Cinnabar & Quispisisa Obsidian
evidence.dateBasis: Ecuador *Spondylus*/*Strombus*, Ayacucho Quispisisa glass & Huancavelica HgS
evidence.summary: Over 1,200 km south of warm Ecuadorian waters, Caral-Supe and Chavín de Huántar centered sacred *mullu* (*Spondylus*) shells alongside Ayacucho obsidian and Huancavelica red cinnabar.
evidence.limits: Intermediate coastal balsa and mountain camelid relay stops leave lighter archaeological signatures.

evidence.title: La Hueca / Sorcé (Vieques) & Trants (Montserrat): Caribbean Saladoid–Huecoid Lapidary
evidence.dateBasis: Raman–PIXE mineral matching of Amazonian nephrite, amethyst & carnelian
evidence.summary: South American canoeists settled the Lesser Antilles and Puerto Rico carrying Amazonian nephrite frog pendants, amethyst, turquoise, and carnelian up the island chain.
evidence.limits: Geological sourcing across South American vs. Central American jadeites remains refined iteratively.

evidence.title: Aboriginal Australian & Papuan Sahul Genomes: ~58–50 ka Divergence & Long Isolation
evidence.dateBasis: Whole-genome coalescent & long-chronology mtDNA/Y models
evidence.summary: Descendants of an early southern Eurasian Out-of-Africa branch (~58–50 ka) who crossed Wallacea into Sahul remained genetically isolated from Eurasian and American farmers until the mid-Holocene—producing distinct Y, mtDNA, and autosomal drift.
evidence.limits: Late Holocene gene flow affected northeastern Torres Strait margins, not western continental Australia.

evidence.title: Arid Interior Barrier: Strong NE vs. SW Aboriginal Australian Genetic Drift (35–10 ka)
evidence.dateBasis: Whole-genome Fst & 50,000-year regional mitogenome phylogeography
evidence.summary: Expanding Lake Mungo, Western Desert, and coastal mitogenomes plus 2023 deep nuclear sequencing show Australia's central deserts drove striking internal genetic drift—generating strong divergence between southwest, northeast, and Tiwi island populations even within Australia.
evidence.limits: Sampling sparsity across central-western deserts reflects colonial displacement rather than empty Pleistocene ranges.

evidence.title: Papua New Guinea Highlands: Extreme Isolation Drift & 4–6% Dual Denisovan Ancestry
evidence.dateBasis: 929-genome Simons/HUGO panels & Papuan regulatory archaic maps
evidence.summary: Steep tropical valleys across New Guinea created stronger valley-to-valley genetic differentiation than across whole Eurasian subcontinents, paired with 4–6% archaic DNA drawn from two deeply diverged Denisovan populations.
evidence.limits: Dated Pleistocene Highland skeletons are rare beneath volcanic/rainforest soils.

evidence.title: Philippine Ayta Magbukon & Wallacea: Record Denisovan Introgression & Independent Contact
evidence.dateBasis: Modern Philippine Negrito & Wallacean genome-wide D-statistics
evidence.summary: Exceeding even Australian and Papuan proportions in some analyses, Ayta communities of Luzon retain ~30–40% higher Denisovan ancestry than Papuans relative to later Austronesian admixture, pointing toward archaic Wallacean/Philippine Denisovan contact.
evidence.limits: No archaic genome from Island Southeast Asia itself has yet been sequenced.

evidence.title: Andaman Islands (Onge / Jarawa): Deep Basal Australasian Drift Preserved Without Mainland Mixing
evidence.dateBasis: Ancient & modern Australasian–South Asian genomic comparisons
evidence.summary: Sharing deep common ancestry with ancestral South Indians (ASI) and early eastern Eurasians before later mainland agricultural waves swamped coastal South Asia, Andaman islanders record profound bottleneck drift and low Denisovan proportions compared to Sahul.
evidence.limits: High Andaman genetic drift mimics rapid branch elongation in unrooted phylogenetic trees.

evidence.title: Beringian Standstill & Serial Founder Bottleneck: Why Americas Hold Lowest Genetic Diversity
evidence.dateBasis: Upward Sun River (USR1) ~11.5 ka genome, mtDNA/Y-chr coalescent & SNP heterozygosity
evidence.summary: Pause and isolation in glacial Beringia for several millennia before ~15 ka ice-corridor and coastal openings trimmed global autosomal heterozygosity to its planetary minimum while generating private Beringian–American founding variants.
evidence.limits: Submerged central Beringian lowlands prevent recovery of Pleistocene Beringian camps themselves.

evidence.title: Ancestral Native American Origin: East Asian + Ancient North Eurasian (Mal'ta) Admixture
evidence.dateBasis: Ancient Siberia–Alaska diploid genomes & Y-chromosome haplogroup Q coalescent
evidence.summary: Ancient DNA reveals Native Americans are NOT direct isolated African/Australian migrants nor pure East Asians: ~30–40% of their ancestry descends from Upper Paleolithic Ancient North Eurasians (shared remotely with Bronze-Age Europeans!) mixed ~20–24 ka with an East Asian branch.
evidence.limits: Exact geographic meeting zone between Lena, Amur, and Beringia remains pinned by scarce LGM skeletons.

evidence.title: Anzick-1 Clovis & Rapid Hemispheric Branching Across North and South America (~16–13 ka)
evidence.dateBasis: Anzick-1 ~12.8 ka genome & 91-genome pan-American transect
evidence.summary: Splitting ~16–15 ka south of the Cordilleran–Laurentide ice sheets into Northern Native American (NNA) and Southern Native American (SNA) clades, founder groups swept all the way to Tierra del Fuego within two millennia—amplifying strong South American micro-drift.
evidence.limits: Small Pleistocene coastal sample size leaves early Pacific-route diversity partially unsampled.

evidence.title: Population Y Signal: Australasian Genetic Affinity in Suruí, Karitiana & Lagoa Santa
evidence.dateBasis: Whole-genome D/f4-statistics across Amazonia, Lagoa Santa & Pacific Brazil
evidence.summary: Amazonian Suruí, Karitiana, Xavánte, and ancient Lagoa Santa remains carry a subtle 1–2% excess allele sharing with Indigenous Australians and Papuans compared to other Native Americans—reflecting structured Asian/Beringian ancestral sub-lineages rather than direct trans-Pacific rafts.
evidence.limits: Alternative models test early South American structured substructure vs. coastal South American influxes.

evidence.title: Indigenous American MUC19 & Immune Introgression: Denisovan–Neanderthal DNA Carried Across Beringia
evidence.dateBasis: Ancestral recombination graphs & ancient Mesoamerican/Peruvian archaic haplotypes
evidence.summary: Native Americans inherited ~1.8–2.5% Neanderthal ancestry plus small traces of Denisovan haplotypes via Northeast Eurasia—including positively selected Denisovan-like *MUC19* mucosal-immunity variants rising to high frequency in the Americas.
evidence.limits: High post-1492 European and African admixture can mask low-frequency archaic American tracts unless phased.

evidence.title: Zlatý kůň (~45 ka) & Bacho Kiro: Early Out-of-Africa Neanderthal–Sapiens Hybrid Wave
evidence.dateBasis: Ancient genome phasing of 6-generation Neanderthal ancestors at Bacho Kiro
evidence.summary: Earliest European modern human genomes from Czechia and Bulgaria contain long, unbroken Neanderthal tracts from contacts just 6–8 generations earlier—yet those pioneer European branches left virtually no direct genetic descendants later in Europe.
evidence.limits: Sparse 45–40 ka specimens leave regional extinction vs. assimilation ratios provisional.

evidence.title: Western Hunter-Gatherers (WHG): Post-LGM Drift, Dark Skin & Blue-Eye Alleles (~14–7 ka)
evidence.dateBasis: Loschbour/Villabruna/Cheddar Man high-coverage aDNA & Mesolithic Fst
evidence.summary: Refugia bottlenecks during the Last Glacial Maximum concentrated strong genetic drift in Mesolithic Western Hunter-Gatherers—distinguishing them sharply from contemporary East Asians and Sahul Australians prior to Neolithic farming.
evidence.limits: Small refugia effective population sizes inflated rare allele frequencies across Iberia–Baltic coasts.

evidence.title: Anatolian & Aegean Early Farmers (~9–6 ka): Mass Neolithic Reshaping of European Genomes
evidence.dateBasis: 100+ ancient Neolithic Mediterranean–Danube genomes
evidence.summary: Instead of Europe remaining genetically isolated like Pleistocene Australia, Anatolian Neolithic farmers with distinct Basal Eurasian ancestry expanded across the Balkans, Mediterranean, and Atlantic, reducing Neanderthal proportions slightly while introducing light-skin variants.
evidence.limits: Resurgence of WHG ancestry varied locally (e.g., higher in Middle Neolithic Iberia/France than Balkans).

evidence.title: Pontic–Caspian Yamnaya Herders (~3000 BCE): Completing Europe's Three-Wave Hybrid Genome
evidence.dateBasis: 1,600+ Eurasian Bronze Age genomes & Uralic–Steppe ancient DNA
evidence.summary: Modern Europeans are a relatively recent Bronze Age fusion of three divergent sources (~50% Anatolian Farmer, ~30–40% Yamnaya Steppe—which carried Ancient North Eurasian Mal'ta ancestry!—and ~10–20% WHG), explaining why Europeans and Native Americans secretly share ~15–20% distant ANE kinship.
evidence.limits: Steppe contribution declines southward into Mediterranean Sardinia and Greece.

evidence.title: Levant & Zagros Basal Eurasian Ghost Lineage: Why Europeans Carry Slightly Less Neanderthal DNA
evidence.dateBasis: Quantitative Neanderthal tract modeling across Near East, Europe & East Asia
evidence.summary: An unsampled 'Basal Eurasian' branch that split early before major Out-of-Africa Neanderthal contact later fed Near Eastern farmers and spread into Europe (~9–7 ka), subtly diluting European Neanderthal proportions (~1.8%) below East Asian levels (~2.1–2.4%).
evidence.limits: No pure Basal Eurasian genome lacking non-African admixture has been sequenced yet.

evidence.title: Southern African Khoe-San: Deepest Living Human Split (~250–200 ka) & Peak Diversity
evidence.dateBasis: Simons/929 diverse genomes deep coalescent & southern aDNA
evidence.summary: Holding the deepest basal divergences among living *Homo sapiens*, Khoe-San groups remind us that genetic differences between two African populations can exceed the difference between Europeans and Aboriginal Australians because only one subset left Africa.
evidence.limits: Holocene Bantu and Khoe pastoralist gene flow later admixed with northern Kalahari groups.

evidence.title: Central African Rainforest Foragers: Deep Pleistocene Divergence & Ecological Specialization
evidence.dateBasis: Whole-genome demography & Shum Laka ancient DNA comparison
evidence.summary: Central African Baka, Biaka, and Mbuti rainforest forager ancestors diverged from other African lineages >100 ka, showing strong long-term effective population stability and physiological adaptation inside closed Congo Basin canopies.
evidence.limits: Humid tropical forest soils yielded zero pre-Holocene human skeletons prior to Shum Laka (8–3 ka).

evidence.title: West African Archaic 'Ghost' Hominin Introgression (2–19% Deeply Diverged DNA)
evidence.dateLabel: Archaic split >500 ka; gene flow ~124–40 ka or later
evidence.dateBasis: Unadmixed outgroup SFS-ABC modeling in Yoruba, Esan & Mende genomes
evidence.summary: Without any sequenced sub-Saharan archaic skeleton (heat destroys tropical aDNA), statistical allele-frequency models reveal 2–19% genetic contribution inside modern West African genomes from an archaic *Homo* ghost lineage that split before Neanderthals and modern humans.
evidence.limits: Timing of African ghost introgression may span multiple Middle-to-Late Pleistocene bouts.

evidence.title: Eurasian Back-to-Africa Gene Flow Carrying Neanderthal DNA Into African Genomes
evidence.dateBasis: IBDmix & archaic-caller detection of Neanderthal segments in Africa
evidence.summary: Reversing earlier assumptions that sub-Saharan Africans have zero Neanderthal ancestry, sensitive haplotype callers reveal ~0.3–0.5% Neanderthal segments brought into Africa by back-migrating Levant/Eurasian pastoralists and traders—meaning literally every human group shares archaic ancestry.
evidence.limits: East Africa shows elevated Eurasian–Neanderthal tracks (~1–1.5%) compared to West Africa (~0.3%).

evidence.title: East African Origin Benchmark: Highest Heterozygosity Before Out-of-Africa Bottleneck
evidence.dateBasis: Global heterozygosity & linkage-disequilibrium decay vs. waypoint distance from East Africa
evidence.summary: Across 142–929 global populations, genetic diversity decays smoothly and linearly (r² > 0.75) with walking distance from eastern/southern Africa—confirming the Serial Founder Effect rather than independent multi-regional origins.
evidence.limits: Colonial mobility slightly flattens steep slope gradients around coastal trading hubs.

evidence.title: Tibetan Plateau EPAS1: Archaic Denisovan Allele Driving High-Altitude Hypoxia Survival
evidence.dateBasis: Haplotype-length Denisovan *EPAS1* sweep modeling across 40+ Tibetan genomes
evidence.summary: Tibetan highlanders carry a 5-SNP Denisovan *EPAS1* haplotype preventing dangerous blood-thickening above 4,000 meters—proving interbreeding with locally adapted archaic hominins gave expanding *Homo sapiens* ready-made physiological survival kits.
evidence.limits: Recombination eroded neutral flanking markers leaving a compact selected core segment.

evidence.title: East Asia 160 ka Synthesis: Two Denisovan Pulses & Elevated Neanderthal Ancestry
evidence.dateBasis: Tianyuan–Harbin ancient DNA & East Asian archaic segment callers
evidence.summary: Present-day East Asians retain ~20% more Neanderthal ancestry than modern Europeans (often explained by extra secondary contact + absence of European Basal Eurasian dilution) plus signals of two distinct Denisovan introgression episodes.
evidence.limits: Whether extra Neanderthal DNA arrived during secondary Asian expansion or later dilution in Europe remains modeled jointly.

evidence.title: Mainland & Island SE Asia Non-African Diversification Hub (~65–45 ka)
evidence.dateBasis: Y-chromosome C/D/F/K/NO/P radiations & global deep tree dating
evidence.summary: Once out of Africa, rapid branching across South and Southeast Asia spawned the foundational Y-chromosome macro-haplogroups that subsequently diverged northwest into Europe, south into Sahul Australia, and northeast into Beringia.
evidence.limits: Mid-Holocene Austroasiatic and Austronesian expansions reshaped mainland lowland autosomal profiles.

evidence.title: Global Adaptive Introgression: Neanderthal/Denisovan Immune & Skin Traits Across Continents
evidence.dateBasis: Ancestral Recombination Graph scans of *HLA*, *TLR*, *OAS*, and cardiovascular pathways
evidence.summary: Across Europe, Asia, and Oceania, purifying selection purged deleterious archaic DNA from regulatory/nervous deserts while repeatedly preserving archaic *HLA*, *TLR*, skin keratin, and angiogenesis immune genes conferring pathogen defenses.
evidence.limits: Adaptive vs. neutral archaic segments require careful background-selection simulations.

waves.title: Bering Strait & Interior Alaska Obsidian Exchange (Krasnoye–Batza Téna–Aleutians)
waves.summary: Caribou hunters and Norton–Aleutian skin-boat mariners exchanged Batza Téna, Okmok, and Chukotka Krasnoye obsidian across Alaska and Bering Strait narrows.
waves.limits: Coastal sea-ice and Bering Strait waters prevent direct shoreline recovery of early boats.

waves.title: Pacific Northwest Coast–Plateau Arc: Mount Edziza Obsidian, Fraser Nephrite & Dentalium Shell
waves.summary: Down glacier-fed canyons and up cedar-canoe inlets, Mount Edziza obsidian, Fraser Canyon nephrite celts, and Vancouver Island *Dentalium* shells knitted together coast and Columbia Plateau.
waves.limits: Woodland soil acidity limits non-mineral organics along middle river stations.

waves.title: California–Great Basin Trans-Sierra Spine: Channel Islands Olivella & Sierra–Coso Obsidian
waves.summary: Cross-Sierra trails carried Catalina steatite, coastal *Olivella* beads, and Casa Diablo–Coso–Napa obsidian between Pacific shellmounds and Great Basin wetland caves.
waves.limits: Mountain snowpasses closed trans-Sierra trails seasonally from autumn through late spring.

waves.title: Plains, Old Copper & Labrador Ramah Chert Continental Network
waves.summary: Ice-margin bands and Archaic miners circulated Knife River flint, Superior native copper, and northern Labrador Ramah Chert across 3,000 kilometers of Plains, Great Lakes, and Atlantic bays.
waves.limits: Represents distinct regional exchange horizons overlapping chronologically across northern North America.

waves.title: Poverty Point Late Archaic Riverine Web (Ouachita–Ozarks–Appalachians–Gulf Coast)
waves.summary: Monumental Louisiana fisher-foragers integrated metric tons of Arkansas novaculite/quartz, Missouri galena, Appalachian soapstone, copper beads, and Gulf Coast whelks.
waves.limits: Multiple riverine tributaries supplied seasonal gathering events rather than standing markets.

waves.title: Hopewell Interaction Sphere (Yellowstone–Bear Gulch–Cobalt–Ohio–Blue Ridge–Florida Gulf)
waves.summary: Scioto Valley earthwork centers exchanged Yellowstone and Idaho obsidian, Lake Superior copper, Ontario silver, Appalachian mica, grizzly teeth, and Florida Gulf *Busycon* whelk.
waves.limits: Peak continental exotic inflow clusters intensely between ~100 BCE and 250 CE.

waves.title: Greater Southwest Early Maize, Sea of Cortez Shell & Mogollon Obsidian Corridor
waves.summary: Domesticated maize moved northward from western Mexico into Santa Cruz canal towns paired with Sea of Cortez *Glycymeris*/*Olivella* shells and Colorado Plateau–Mogollon obsidian.
waves.limits: Pre-ceramic desert caravan stops preserve sparse architectural visibility.

waves.title: Olmec Gulf Coast Obsidian, Motagua Jadeite & Oaxaca Magnetite Network
waves.summary: Early–Middle Preclassic Olmec towns imported Hidalgo green glass, San José Mogote optical magnetite mirrors, Chiapas ilmenite tons, and Guatemalan Motagua jadeite.
waves.limits: Lowland Tabasco humidity dissolves organic cacao/rubber cargoes outside deep bog caches.

waves.title: Preclassic Maya–Costa Rica Highlands-to-Sea Obsidian, Jadeite & Marine Shell Spine
waves.summary: El Chayal, San Martín Jilotepeque, and Ixtepeque obsidian flowed down Usumacinta rivers and Amatique Bay coastal canoes to Petén, Belize, and south toward Nicoya greenstone artisans.
waves.limits: Swamp-margin ports along eastern Yucatán remain under active marine survey.

waves.title: Equatorial Pacific–Amazonia–Caral Maritime Spine: Spondylus *Mullu* & *Theobroma cacao*
waves.summary: Crossing ecological zones from Upper Amazon cacao plazas (Santa Ana–La Florida) and Guayas reefs to Caral-Supe, Chavín, and West Mexico coastal worlds, warm-water *Spondylus* was Peru's paramount sacred commodity.
waves.limits: West Mexico maritime extension remains under active comparative testing.

waves.title: Andean Highland–Desert Vertical Caravans: Quispisisa, Huancavelica, Alca, Chivay & Atacama
waves.summary: Llama caravans linked high Ayacucho–Huancavelica–Arequipa obsidian and cinnabar mines with Pacific Paracas–Nasca oases, Titicaca Chiripa mounds, and Atacama–NW Argentina turquoise/cebil networks.
waves.limits: Separate north–central vs. Altiplano–Atacama caravan spheres intersected along Lake Titicaca.

waves.title: Saladoid–Huecoid Trans-Caribbean Sea Arc (Orinoco–Trants Montserrat–Vieques La Hueca)
waves.summary: Oceanic dugout mariners transported mainland South American nephrite *muiraquitã*, amethyst, turquoise, and carnelian from Orinoco shores through Grenada and Montserrat bead workshops to Vieques, Puerto Rico.
waves.limits: Deep open Anegada and Mona passages filtered distinct cultural spheres in later periods.

waves.title: Out-of-Africa Serial Founder Effect: Global Heterozygosity Decay & Continental Drift
waves.summary: Successive small founder bottlenecks moving away from Africa trimmed heterozygosity linearly with geographic distance—maximizing diversity inside Africa and yielding peak drift/low heterozygosity in remote Sahul and South America.
waves.limits: Subsequent Holocene farming and steppe expansions partially overwrote earlier spatial clines across Eurasia.

waves.title: Sahul Early Divergence & ~45 ka Continental Isolation of Australia and New Guinea
waves.summary: Branching early out of Africa/South Asia into Wallacea and absorbing heavy Denisovan DNA en route to Sahul, Aboriginal Australian and Papuan ancestors remained cut off from Eurasia for ~45,000 years—producing deep continental genetic divergence.
waves.limits: Exact Wallacean island mixing loci remain inferred statistically rather than recovered as fossils.

waves.title: Australian Arid-Interior Drift Barrier: 50 ka Geographic Isolation Across Deserts
waves.summary: Rapid ~50 ka coastal settlement followed by central desert aridity anchored long-term regional kin stability and intense internal genetic drift between Western Desert, Northeast Queensland, Tiwi, and Southwest Australian lineages.
waves.limits: Holocene Pama-Nyungan linguistic spread moved primarily via cultural/gene diffusion with small effective inputs.

waves.title: Dual-to-Multiple Denisovan Introgression Waves Across East Asia, Philippines & Sahul
waves.summary: Genomic haplotype clustering proves modern humans encountered at least two-to-three deeply diverged Denisovan populations—contributing *EPAS1* altitude adaptation to Tibetans and ~3–6% ancestry across Australia, New Guinea, and Philippine Ayta.
waves.limits: Southern Denisovan fossil remains outside Siberia/Tibet have not yet yielded direct aDNA.

waves.title: Global Neanderthal Interbreeding & Back-to-Africa Persistence
waves.dateLabel: Main pulse ~50–45 ka; later back-flow into Africa
waves.summary: Starting primarily ~50–45 ka in Southwest Asia with additional eastern contacts—and later carried back into sub-Saharan Africa via Eurasian pastoralists—Neanderthal DNA reshaped *HLA*/viral immunity and lipid/skin traits globally.
waves.limits: Secondary minor pulses across Europe and East Asia remain debated relative to Basal Eurasian dilution.

waves.title: European Three-Wave Genomic Synthesis: WHG + Anatolian Farmers + Yamnaya Steppe
waves.summary: Unlike Australia's long continental isolation, Europe was genetically remade twice by mass migrations—first Anatolian farmers (~7000–4000 BCE) and then Yamnaya Steppe herders (~3000–2000 BCE)—creating today's tripartite European ancestry.
waves.limits: Steppe vs. Anatolian fractions trace clear north–south geographical gradients.

waves.title: East Asian + Ancient North Eurasian (Mal'ta) Fusion Creating Ancestral Native Americans
waves.summary: Ancestral Native Americans merged ~60–70% Northeast Asian ancestry with ~30–40% Mal'ta-related Ancient North Eurasian ancestry before Beringian isolation—a dual root completely absent from Sahul Australia.
waves.limits: Kolyma/Yana ancient genomes bridge Siberian stages of this western–eastern fusion.

waves.title: Beringian Standstill & Rapid South American Micro-Drift Radiation
waves.summary: Emerging out of a tight Beringian bottleneck south of ice sheets ~15.5 ka, founding clades diversified down the Pacific and interior valleys to Patagonia within ~2,000 years—yielding strong regional drift in Amazonia and Patagonia.
waves.limits: Early coastal glacial drownings limit archaeological visibility of Pacific entry stations.

waves.title: Population Y Australasian Affinity Across Amazonia & Lagoa Santa
waves.summary: Ancient and modern Brazilian–Amazonian genomes retain a subtle ~1–2% Australo-Melanesian (*Population Y*) genetic affinity relative to other Native Americans, pointing toward deep Asian/Beringian population structure surviving south of Panama.
waves.limits: Competing hypotheses debate an early Pacific-coast wave vs. structured UP Siberian ancestry.

waves.title: West/Central African Ghost Hominin Admixture & Deep Continental Structuring
waves.dateLabel: Deep structure ~250 ka; ghost pulses ~124–40 ka
waves.summary: Far before Eurasia or Australia saw a single *Homo sapiens* footprint, structured African populations swapped genes across savanna–rainforest transitions while absorbing 2–19% DNA from an unsampled archaic African hominin lineage.
waves.limits: High equatorial temperatures destroy ancient DNA in Middle Stone Age African fossils.
